d.app.disclaimer: FamSurvivor helps you get organized. It does not replace instructions from the authorities or medical advice: in a real emergency, follow official instructions.
d.home.welcomeLead: In two minutes you'll know how much water and food your family needs, what's missing and who does what if everything goes down.
d.home.localFirst: Local-first: no server and no accounts. What you enter stays on this phone.
d.home.legacyFound: We found data from the previous version of FamSurvivor in this browser.
d.home.legacyDone: Data brought over. Check the quantities in your supplies.
d.home.exampleBody: This data is made up to show how the app works.
d.home.exampleClearBody: The example data is deleted and you start with a blank household.
d.home.exampleLoaded: Example loaded. The data is made up.
d.home.standalone: You're using the single-file test version: it can't be installed and has no offline mode of its own. For that, use the published version. Back up what you enter.
d.home.memOnly: This browser doesn't allow saving data (private mode?). What you enter is lost when you close it: export a backup from Settings.
d.home.iosWarn: On iPhone and iPad, if you don't add the app to the home screen, Safari may delete its data after about 7 days without use. Install it or make a backup.
d.home.quota: There's no space left on the phone to save. Free up space and export a backup.
d.home.saveError: The last change couldn't be saved. Export a backup just in case.
d.how.intro: Self-sufficiency is the lowest of your critical resources: food for two weeks is no use if the water only lasts two days. Expired items don't count.
d.how.water: Water: you have {have} L and your household uses {perDay} L a day.
d.how.heat: Includes the extra for extreme heat.
d.how.food: Food: you have {have} kcal and your household needs {perDay} kcal a day.
d.how.meds: Medication: units you have divided by doses per day; the one that runs out first counts.
d.how.energy: Power: you have {have} usable Wh and use {perDay} Wh a day ({phones} phone(s) in power-saving mode plus charged devices).
d.how.pets: Pets: you have {have} kg of food and they eat {perDay} g a day.
d.how.noKcal_one: {n} food item has no calories entered: it isn't counted. Edit it to include it.
d.how.noKcal_other: {n} food items have no calories entered: they aren't counted. Edit them to include them.
d.how.params: One ration equals {ration} kcal. Water level: {comfort}.
d.today.soon_one: {n} item expires in less than 30 days: use it and restock
d.today.soon_other: {n} items expire in less than 30 days: use them and restock
d.setup.title: Your household in 2 minutes
d.setup.intro: This is enough to calculate. Later you can fill in each member if you want. We don't ask for names or IDs.
d.setup.tooMany: Up to {max} members in total, counting pets.
d.setup.needOne: Add at least one person or pet.
d.setup.done: Done. You now have your calculation and a shopping list.
d.hh.title: Your household
d.hh.zoneHint: Optional and approximate. The app doesn't use GPS or addresses.
d.hh.regionHint: Used to suggest the most common hazards. You adjust them afterwards.
d.hh.regionOnlyAR: For now, regional hazard profiles are for Argentina only. In other countries you start from the generic profile: review and adjust each hazard for your area.
d.hh.pump: Our water depends on an electric pump
d.hh.tankNote: You also have about {l} L in the tank. It doesn't count as drinking water: make it safe before drinking.
d.hh.container: Size of the water jug you buy (liters)
d.hh.containerHint: Used to tell you how many jugs you're missing.
d.hh.phonesHint: Leave it empty to count one for each person aged 14 or over.
d.hh.comfortHint: Minimum: drinking and cooking. Recommended: adds {l} L per person per day for basic hygiene.
d.mem.title: Members
d.mem.anon: {people} and {pets}. Use nicknames or roles: never full names or ID numbers.
d.mem.empty: You haven't added any members yet.
d.mem.formIntro: Everything is optional except the nickname. Health details stay only on this phone, can be hidden and aren't printed unless you ask.
d.mem.aliasHint: For example: Mom, Grandpa, Adult 2, Rocco.
d.mem.weightHint: Optional. For pets it adjusts water and food.
d.mem.conditionsHint: Only mark what changes your preparation. The app doesn't give medical advice.
d.mem.powerW: Power use of the electrical device (watts)
d.mem.powerHint: It's on the device's label. Talk to your power company and your doctor about a backup.
d.mem.needs: Per day: {l} L of water · {kcal} kcal
d.mem.petNeeds: Per day: {l} L of water · {g} g of dry food
d.mem.delBody: Their roles in the plan become “unassigned” so you can reassign them.
d.med.intro: Only to know how many days it lasts. The app doesn't give doses: ask your doctor or pharmacy how to keep a supply.
d.med.name: Name
d.med.coldHint: If the power goes out, you'll need a plan to keep it cold. Ask your pharmacy.
d.threat.title: Hazards in your area
d.threat.intro: Say how likely each one is where you live. The most relevant ones stay on top.
d.threat.applyBody: It replaces the levels you set. It's a starting point: adjust them to your neighborhood.
d.pantry.empty: Your supplies are empty. Add what you already have at home.
d.pantry.emptyPillar: You haven't added anything to this pillar yet.
d.item.presetHint: Fills in the details for you. You can correct them afterwards.
d.item.name: What it is
d.item.litersHint: A 6 L jug: type 6. Without this it isn't counted as water.
d.item.petHint: Enter it in kg to calculate how many days it lasts.
d.item.kcalHint: It's on the package. If you enter “rations”, one ration is 700 kcal.
d.item.whHint: A 10,000 mAh power bank is about 37 Wh.
d.item.expiresHint: Optional. With a date, the app warns you before it expires.
d.cash.title: Cash
d.cash.intro: Optional. If you enter it, it stays only on this phone and you can hide it on screen.
d.cash.daily: Estimated daily spending in an emergency
d.cash.onHandHint: Leave it empty if you'd rather not write it down.
d.cash.hint: Small bills are better: there may be no change.
d.shop.title: Shopping list for {days} days
d.shop.intro: It's based on what you're missing to reach your goal. Buy a little at a time, with your usual shopping.
d.shop.empty: You have everything for your goal.
d.shop.agua: {liters} L of water (≈ {count} jugs of {size} L)
d.shop.bebe: For the baby: about {diapers} diapers, their food or formula and safe water to prepare it
d.shop.medNote: For medication, talk to your doctor or pharmacy: they can tell you how to keep a supply.
d.shop.celiac: Someone in your household has celiac disease: choose gluten-free products.
d.shop.allergy: Someone in your household has food allergies: check the ingredients.
d.maint.title: Regular checks
d.maint.intro: Stored items expire and batteries run down. These checks keep your preparation up to date.
d.maint.label: What to check
d.maint.doneToast: Noted. We'll show it again when it's due.
d.maint.doneDrill: Noted. If you want to time it, do it from Plan → Practice.
d.maint.icsDone: File downloaded. Open it to add it to your calendar.
d.maint.honest: The app can't send you notifications while it's closed. To have your phone remind you, add the checks to your calendar with the .ics file: they become recurring events with an alarm.
d.plan.lead: So every member knows what to do, where and when, even if you can't communicate.
d.plan.pointsIntro: Choose places everyone knows and that won't change.
d.plan.pointAPh: For example: the square, by the flagpole
d.plan.pointAHint: To get out of the house quickly: a fire, a gas leak.
d.plan.pointBHint: In case you can't go back to the neighborhood.
d.plan.pointCHint: An alternative, for example in another city.
d.plan.wait: How long to wait at Point A
d.plan.rule: If we're not together and there's no communication: go to Point A, wait {hours} h and then go to Point B.
d.plan.commIntro: Agree on fixed times to turn on phones and the radio. That saves battery and you'll overlap.
d.plan.windowText: Communication window: every {every} min, from minute :{minute}.
d.plan.commNote: What to do in the window
d.plan.commNotePh: For example: turn on the AM radio and check texts
d.plan.smsFirst: Texts first: when the network is overloaded, a short message often gets through even if a call doesn't. Say who you are, where you are, how you are and where you're going.
d.plan.outIntro: Someone in another city that everyone checks in with. Sometimes it's easier to reach someone far away than nearby.
d.plan.noPhones: There are no phone numbers loaded for your country. Add the ones for your area.
d.plan.paper: Write these numbers down on paper: if your phone runs out of battery, the contact list is useless. You can print them from Settings.
d.plan.rolesIntro: One task per person, with a place and a moment. Something that can be done without asking.
d.plan.rolesEmpty: There are no tasks for this situation yet.
d.role.intro: Write it as a short instruction that makes sense under stress.
d.role.actionPh: For example: shut off the gas and take the documents
d.role.wherePh: For example: valve next to the meter
d.role.whenPh: For example: as soon as we decide to leave
d.role.templateDone: Template added. Adapt it to your home.
d.dist.title: Does everyone know?
d.dist.intro: A plan only works if everyone has it and has practiced it. Tick the boxes as you go.
d.drill.title: Drill
d.drill.intro: Practice with the clock running, as if it were real. Each step you tick saves its time.
d.drill.failedQ: What went wrong or was hard?
d.drill.failedHint: For example: we couldn't find the flashlight; nobody knew where to shut off the gas.
d.drill.ownerQ: Who will work on improving it?
d.drill.saved: Drill saved. The next one is scheduled.
d.guide.title: Quick guides
d.guide.intro: To have at hand offline. They don't replace a first aid course or official instructions.
d.em.chooseLead: Choose the situation. You'll see the steps in order and your details at hand. Works offline.
d.em.noRoles: No tasks entered for this situation.
d.em.water: You have {have} L. At {perDay} L a day it lasts {days} days.
d.em.medsNote: Take your medication with you and keep up your usual treatment.
d.em.finishBody: You did {done} of {total} steps. A record is saved and the checklist closes.
d.em.minimize: Back to the app (still in progress)
d.em.cancelDrillTitle: Cancel the drill without saving it?
d.em.logged: Record saved. When you can, restock what you used.
d.print.title: Print
d.print.intro: Paper never runs out of battery. It prints in black and white.
d.print.privacyHint: Sensitive details are only printed if you tick them. Think about who might see that piece of paper.
d.print.walletHint: Cut along the dotted line and fold in half. One card per person.
d.print.backpackIntro: One bag per person, near the exit. Check it every six months.
d.print.backpackNote: Adapt it to your family and to what your civil protection agency recommends.
d.print.footer: Printed on {date}. It does not replace instructions from the authorities.
d.bk.title: Backup
d.bk.intro: Your data lives only on this phone. If it breaks, gets lost or you clear the browser data, it's gone. Save a backup and share it with the other phones in your household.
d.bk.plainBody: Anyone who opens the file will be able to read it, including medication and cash if you entered them. To send it by messaging app, the encrypted backup is better.
d.bk.encIntro: The file is encrypted with 256-bit AES-GCM; the key comes from your passphrase with PBKDF2 ({iter} iterations).
d.import.choose: Replace deletes what you have now and keeps the backup. Merge keeps what you have and adds what's missing. This phone's settings don't change.
d.import.v1: This is a backup from the previous version. It was converted to the new format: supply quantities were free text, so check them. If it was the original demo, its data is example data.
d.import.example: This backup is marked as example data.
d.import.err.too_big: The file is larger than 1 MB: it doesn't look like a FamSurvivor backup.
d.import.err.bad_json: The file is damaged or isn't a backup: it couldn't be read.
d.import.err.not_object: The file doesn't have the format of a FamSurvivor backup.
d.import.err.unknown_shape: We don't recognize this file as a FamSurvivor backup.
d.import.err.incomplete: The backup is missing parts (household, members or supplies). Nothing was imported.
d.import.err.newer: This backup is from a newer version of the app. Update FamSurvivor and try again.
d.priv.title: Privacy
d.priv.encOnBody: What's saved on this phone is encrypted. The key only exists while the app is unlocked.
d.priv.encOffBody: Data is saved on this phone without encryption: anyone who unlocks it and opens the browser could read it. You can protect it with a passphrase.
d.priv.enableIntro: It uses 256-bit AES-GCM and PBKDF2 with {iter} iterations. You'll type the passphrase every time you open the app.
d.priv.passHint: Use four words or more. A short PIN can be guessed by trying combinations if someone copies your data.
d.priv.ack: I understand that if I forget the passphrase there's no way to recover the data
d.priv.weak: It's too short or only numbers. Use at least 8 characters; four words is better.
d.priv.disableBody: Data will be saved on this phone without encryption again.
d.priv.lockOnHide: Lock when leaving the app for more than 30 seconds
d.priv.lockHint: During an emergency in progress the app doesn't lock by itself, so you don't lose the checklist.
d.priv.hideHint: Covers health, medication and cash until you tap “Show details”. It isn't encryption: it just keeps prying eyes away.
d.priv.noCrypto: This browser, or this way of opening the app, doesn't offer encryption (HTTPS is required). Encrypted backups aren't available here.
d.priv.wipeBody: Everything entered on this phone is deleted. This can't be undone. If you want to keep it, export a backup first.
d.lock.body: Your data is encrypted. Type your passphrase to open it.
d.lock.noRecovery: Without the passphrase there's no way to recover the data. If you lost it, clear the site data in your browser and import a backup.
d.look.title: Appearance
d.look.themeHint: Automatic follows your phone: day when it's light, night in the dark. Day is easier to read in sunlight. Battery saver uses pure black and turns off shadows and animations: on OLED screens it uses much less power.
d.lang.title: Language
d.lang.hint: Changes the app's text. What you wrote yourself stays as it is.
d.inst.title: Installation and version
d.inst.android: On Android: open the browser menu and choose “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”.
d.inst.ios: On iPhone or iPad: open it in Safari, tap Share and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
d.inst.mem: Only in memory: lost when closed
d.inst.notPersisted: the browser could clear it if space runs low
d.inst.offlinePending: Not yet: open it once more while online
d.inst.offlineNo: Not available in the single-file version
d.inst.updateFound: A new version is available. Your data isn't touched.
d.inst.upToDate: You already have the latest version.
d.inst.push: The app doesn't use push notifications, analytics or third-party services.
d.src.title: Sources and how it's calculated
d.src.intro: Content reviewed on {date}. Each figure shows where it comes from and whether it could be checked against the official source.
d.src.linksNote: Links open in the browser and need a connection. The app itself doesn't connect to any site.
d.src.f.water: Water per person per day: {adult} L for drinking from age 9, + 1 L for cooking, + {heat} L if you set extreme heat at medium or high, + {hyg} L for hygiene at the Recommended level. Pregnancy adds 0.5 L and breastfeeding 1 L.
d.src.f.kids: Children: babies {a} L (includes water to prepare their food), ages 1 to 3 {b} L, ages 4 to 8 {c} L, plus 1 L for cooking from age 1. Heat adds 0.5 L.
d.src.f.pets: Pets: dogs {dog} ml per kg per day, cats {cat} ml per kg, with a minimum of {min} L. In hot weather, 25% more.
d.src.f.food: Food: {kcal} kcal per person per day from age 9; 1,400 from 4 to 8; 1,000 from 1 to 3; 700 for babies. Pregnancy +300 and breastfeeding +500. One ration = {ration} kcal.
d.src.f.petfood: Pet food: resting energy (70 × weight^0.75) × 1.6 for dogs or 1.2 for cats, at {k} kcal per gram of dry food. It's a guide: check the table on the package.
d.src.f.meds: Medication: days covered = units you have ÷ doses per day. The app never suggests doses.
d.src.f.energy: Power: {phone} Wh per phone per day in power-saving mode, plus watts × hours of each charged device. For power banks, {eff}% is counted because of losses.
d.src.f.cash: Cash: the daily spending you estimate × goal days.
d.src.f.autonomy: Self-sufficiency: the lowest value among water, food, medication (if entered), pet food (if you have pets) and power (only if someone depends on electrical equipment). Totals are rounded up; days, down.
d.src.f.expiry: Expiry: expired, less than 30 days, less than 90 days or up to date. Expired items don't count as stock.
d.about.title: About
d.about.body: FamilySurvivor (FamSurvivor) helps any household prepare for water or power outages, storms, floods and other emergencies, and have a plan when there's no communication.
d.about.honest: Local-first: no server, no accounts, no tracking. It doesn't ask for names, IDs or exact location.
d.test.title: Self-test

c.Para beber y un extra para cocinar: For drinking, plus extra for cooking
c.Que se pueda comer sin heladera ni cocin: That can be eaten without a fridge or stove
c.A pilas o a manivela, para escuchar avis: Battery-powered or hand-crank, to hear official alerts
c.Portátil y cargada, con su cable: Portable and charged, with its cable
c.Billetes chicos, por si no andan las tar: Small bills, in case cards don't work
c.Copias y teléfonos anotados en papel: Copies and phone numbers written on paper
c.Lo que le sirve a tu hogar en particular: Whatever your household in particular needs
c.Lavandina apta para desinfectar agua (si: Bleach suitable for disinfecting water (no additives)
c.Copias de documentos en bolsa estanca: Copies of documents in a waterproof bag
c.Lista de teléfonos en papel: List of phone numbers on paper
c.Copias de documentos y teléfonos anotado: Copies of documents and phone numbers written on paper
c.Probar linterna, radio y batería portáti: Test flashlight, radio and power bank
c.Revisar botiquín y vencimientos de medic: Check the first aid kit and medication expiry dates
c.Revisar el matafuegos (manómetro y recar: Check the fire extinguisher (gauge and refill)
c.Actualizar copias de documentos y teléfo: Update copies of documents and phone numbers
c.Ciberataque a servicios (agua, luz, pago: Cyberattack on services (water, power, payments, phone)
It can cut several services at once. Prioritize water, cash and radio.
c.Guardá agua para los días que te propusi: Store water for the number of days you set as your goal.
c.Tené efectivo en billetes chicos y los t: Keep cash in small bills and phone numbers written on paper.
c.Acordá en familia los puntos de encuentr: Agree on meeting points and the communication window as a family.
c.Informate por radio y canales oficiales;: Get information from the radio and official channels; don't trust chain messages and rumors.
c.Si el agua sigue saliendo, juntá en reci: If water is still running, collect some in clean containers before it's cut off.
c.Usá el celular lo justo: mensajes cortos: Use your phone sparingly: short texts rather than calls.
c.Esperá el aviso oficial antes de volver: Wait for the official notice before drinking tap water again.
c.Reponé lo que usaste y anotá qué te falt: Restock what you used and note what you were missing.
c.Sin luz suele fallar la bomba de agua, e: Without power, the water pump, elevator, fridge and phone charging often fail. Power bank, flashlight and water become more important.
c.Mantené cargada la batería portátil y pr: Keep the power bank charged and test the flashlight and radio once a month.
c.Si alguien depende de un equipo eléctric: If someone depends on electrical equipment, talk to the power company and their doctor about a backup plan.
c.Si tu edificio usa bomba, guardá agua ex: If your building uses a pump, store extra water.
c.No abras la heladera ni el freezer sin n: Don't open the fridge or freezer unless you need to: closed, the fridge keeps food cold for about 4 hours; a full freezer for about 48 hours (24 if half full).
c.Usá linternas. Si prendés velas, nunca l: Use flashlights. If you light candles, never leave them unattended or near curtains.
c.Nunca uses generador, brasero, parrilla: Never use a generator, brazier, grill or gas cylinder to heat indoors: they produce carbon monoxide.
c.Desenchufá los equipos sensibles para pr: Unplug sensitive devices to protect them when the power comes back.
c.Tirá los alimentos perecederos que pasar: Throw away perishable food that has been without refrigeration for more than 4 hours. When in doubt, don't eat it.
Recharge power banks and replace batteries.
c.Con nivel medio o alto, el cálculo suma: At medium or high level, the calculation adds water: +1 L per person per day (+0.5 L for children under 9) and 25% more for pets.
c.Sumá agua a tu reserva y tené sales de r: Add water to your supply and keep oral rehydration salts in the first aid kit.
c.Identificá el ambiente más fresco de la: Find the coolest room in the house.
c.Tomá agua seguido, sin esperar a tener s: Drink water often, without waiting until you're thirsty. Offer water to children and older people.
c.Evitá el sol y el esfuerzo en las horas: Avoid the sun and physical effort during the hottest hours.
c.Ante confusión, desmayo o piel muy calie: If someone is confused, faints or has very hot, dry skin, call emergency services.
c.Suma abrigo y mantas. El mayor riesgo en: Warm clothes and blankets matter more. The biggest risk at home is carbon monoxide.
c.Hacé revisar estufas y calefones por un: Have heaters and water heaters checked by a licensed gas technician.
c.Tené mantas y abrigo a mano. Considerá u: Keep blankets and warm clothes at hand. Consider a carbon monoxide detector.
c.Ventilá siempre el ambiente donde haya u: Always ventilate any room with a gas heater or brazier. Don't use the stove burners or oven for heating.
c.Apagá braseros y estufas a leña antes de: Put out braziers and wood stoves before going to sleep.
c.Dolor de cabeza, mareo o náuseas en un a: Headache, dizziness or nausea in a heated room: go outside and call emergency services.
c.Revisá cañerías y reponé combustible de: Check the pipes and restock fuel safely.
c.Tormenta severa, granizo, viento o torna: Severe storm, hail, wind or tornado
c.Suele traer cortes de luz y anegamientos: It often brings power cuts and flooding. Reinforce flashlight, power bank and documents in a waterproof bag.
c.Asegurá o guardá lo que pueda volarse. L: Secure or put away anything that could blow away. Clear drains and gutters.
c.Seguí los alertas del servicio meteoroló: Follow the alerts from your country's weather service.
c.Quedate adentro, lejos de ventanas. Con: Stay inside, away from windows. In a tornado or very strong wind, go to the lowest, most interior room.
c.No toques cables caídos ni te acerques a: Don't touch fallen wires or go near poles or trees.
c.Si estás en la calle, no cruces calles a: If you're out on the street, don't cross flooded streets.
c.Revisá daños con cuidado. Avisá a la dis: Check for damage carefully. Tell the power company if there are fallen wires.
c.Puede obligarte a evacuar. Prepará mochi: It may force you to evacuate. Prepare a go-bag, documents in a waterproof bag and Point B outside the area.
c.Guardá comida, documentos y botiquín en: Store food, documents and the first aid kit up high.
c.Ubicá la llave de luz y la de gas para c: Find the electricity and gas shut-offs so you can turn them off quickly.
Agree on where to go and which route to take.
c.Cortá la luz y el gas si entra agua. Sub: Turn off the electricity and gas if water gets in. Move to higher ground or evacuate if the authorities say so.
c.No camines ni manejes por agua en movimi: Don't walk or drive through moving water. Don't touch wet wires or appliances.
c.Tomá solo agua segura: embotellada, herv: Drink only safe water: bottled, boiled or treated.
c.El agua de inundación está contaminada:: Floodwater is contaminated: wash and disinfect anything it touched, and treat water before drinking it.
c.No conectes la electricidad hasta que la: Don't turn the electricity back on until the wiring is dry and has been checked.
c.Se resuelve en minutos: lo que cuenta es: It plays out in minutes: what matters is the way out and Point A, not supplies.
c.Mantené libres las salidas. Tené un mata: Keep the exits clear. Have an ABC fire extinguisher at hand and learn how to use it.
c.No sobrecargues enchufes. Acordá dos sal: Don't overload outlets. Agree on two ways out and Point A.
c.Salí ya y llamá a los bomberos desde afu: Get out now and call the fire department from outside. Don't go back in.
c.Si hay humo, avanzá agachado. Tocá las p: If there's smoke, stay low. Touch doors before opening them: if they're hot, find another way out.
c.Entrá solo cuando los bomberos lo autori: Go back in only when the firefighters say so.
c.Incendio forestal o de interfase y humo: Wildfire or wildland-urban interface fire and smoke
c.Puede exigir evacuar con poco aviso. Sum: You may have to evacuate with little warning. Face masks for smoke and a ready go-bag become more important.
c.Mantené despejado de pasto seco y leña e: Keep the area around the house clear of dry grass and firewood.
c.Tené la mochila lista y dos caminos de s: Keep the go-bag ready and two ways out.
c.Si las autoridades indican evacuar, hace: If the authorities say to evacuate, do it immediately.
c.Con humo: quedate adentro con puertas y: With smoke: stay inside with doors and windows closed, and look after anyone with breathing problems.
c.Volvé solo con autorización. Cuidado con: Go back only when authorized. Watch out for embers and weakened trees.
c.Puede cortar agua, luz y gas a la vez. R: It can cut water, power and gas at the same time. Reinforce water, the first aid kit and shoes near the bed.
c.Fijá muebles altos y no cuelgues objetos: Secure tall furniture and don't hang heavy objects over beds.
c.Identificá lugares seguros en cada ambie: Identify safe spots in each room and where to shut off gas, power and water.
c.Agachate, cubrite bajo una mesa firme y: Drop, take cover under a sturdy table and hold on until it stops. Stay away from windows.
c.No uses ascensor ni corras hacia la sali: Don't use the elevator or run for the exit while it's shaking.
c.Si sentís olor a gas, cortá la llave, ve: If you smell gas, close the valve, ventilate and get out. Expect aftershocks.
c.Usá mensajes cortos: las líneas se satur: Use short texts: the lines get overloaded.
c.Suma barbijos, anteojos de protección y: Face masks, protective goggles and covered water become more important.
c.Tené barbijos y anteojos, y forma de tap: Have face masks and goggles, and a way to cover water tanks and containers.
c.Quedate adentro con puertas y ventanas c: Stay inside with doors and windows closed. Protect your nose, mouth and eyes if you go out.
